sentences.text: % 22.03.2023 CRL.M.A. 7574/2023 (for exemption)

1. Exemption allowed, subject to just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ('Cr.P.C') has been filed by the petitioner seeking of quashing of FIR bearing no. 190/2011, registered at Police Station Naraina, Delhi, for offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Manoj Pant, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioner is present before this Court and has been identified by his counsel Ms. Chitrakshi and Investigating Officer (IO) Insp. Jag Mohan from Police Station Naraina, Delhi.

6. Brief facts of the present case are that petitioner was a property dealer and due to some misunderstanding of the facts and circumstances regarding sale of the plot, some dispute had arisen between petitioner and respondent no. 2.
On the complaint of complainant/respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no. 190/2011 was registered at Police Station Naraina, Delhi, for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC against petitioners.

It is further stated that with the intervention of Dharambir Singh vs State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22630950/
1 well-wishers, close friends and respectable persons of the society, petitioner and respondent no. 2 have resolved their disputes amicably vide Settlement Deed dated 10.02.2023.
7.

entities.text: Dharambir Singh vs State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 (through Video Conferencing) who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that he has entered into compromise out of his own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Settlement Deed dated 10.02.2023.
Respondent no. 2 further stated that he has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

8. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

9. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 190/2011, registered at Police Station Naraina, Delhi, for offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed, subject to petitioner depositing a sum of Rs. 5,000/- with the Delhi High Court Advocates Welfare Fund within seven days.

entities.text: Delhi High Court Advocates Welfare Fund
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 10. The present petition stands disposed of.
11. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J MARCH 22, 2023/
